title: IT Certification Guide: Networking, Databases, Data Science & AI
lead: A certification is not a goal — it is a "business card" that shows others what you can do. Here are certifications in four fields — networking, databases (SQL), data science and AI — that you can take in English, or in Japanese with a low language barrier. From free ones you can take today to international ones that help you get a job.

q3: Which field do you want to show?
stepText: Start with a free course or test and earn your first credential. You can put it on your CV and LinkedIn.
The entrance to paid official exams. Student discounts and free-training discounts can keep the cost low.
High-level certifications that are valued in job hunting. Some expect work experience.
tipsH: Check before you take an exam
tips: Fees and exam contents can change. Always check the latest information on the official page before you register.
Register with the same name spelling as on your ID (e.g. your passport).
Online exams need a camera, a microphone and a stable internet connection. Some exams do not allow anyone else in the room.
Student discounts may require a student ID card or a school email address.
When you pass, save the certificate URL and add it to your CV, LinkedIn and portfolio.

hr_sql.what: Your ability to actually write SQL queries. Three levels: Basic, Intermediate and Advanced.
hr_sql.who: Anyone who can solve the problems on our SQL practice site. The best first certification.
hr_sql.prep: Solve HackerRank's SQL practice problems first. The test is timed, so practise with a timer. Practise in the same format, with a 30-minute mock test, in "HackerRank practice" on our SQL practice site.

hr_py.what: Your ability to write basic Python programs.
hr_py.who: Anyone who knows basic Python (lists, functions, if statements).
hr_py.prep: Practise HackerRank's Python problems within a time limit.

fcc_db.what: Basics of SQL, databases, Bash and Git. You earn it with 5 projects and a 50-question exam.
fcc_db.who: Anyone who wants to learn SQL in English step by step, by building projects.
fcc_db.prep: Work through the lessons in order, finish the 5 projects, then take the exam.

fcc_py.what: Python basics. You earn it with projects and a final exam.
fcc_py.who: Anyone who wants to learn Python for free by building projects.
fcc_py.prep: Follow the lessons and projects, then take the final exam.

g_da.what: The whole data analysis process (ask, prepare, process, analyse, visualise, share), using spreadsheets, SQL, Tableau and Python.
g_da.who: Anyone who wants to learn data analysis systematically from English videos.
g_da.prep: About 6 months at 10 hours a week. Apply for financial aid before starting the free trial.

py_intro.what: Introductory Python knowledge. Multiple choice, so knowledge matters more than Japanese.
py_intro.who: Python beginners who want a Japanese certification.
py_intro.prep: This exam started in 2026. Check the schedule and details on the official page.

py_basic.what: Basic Python grammar. Most questions are about reading code.
py_basic.who: Anyone who wants a Japanese certification to show Python skills to Japanese companies.
py_basic.prep: Study the official textbook (the Python Tutorial) and practice exams. Multiple choice; pass with 70%.

py_data.what: Basic data analysis knowledge with NumPy, pandas and more.
py_data.who: Anyone who wants to show data analysis skills with a Japanese certification after the Python basic exam.
py_data.prep: Study the official textbook and practice exams. The pandas you use in class helps directly.

dp900.what: Data basics (relational and non-relational databases, analytics) and cloud (Azure) basics.
dp900.who: Anyone who wants a first official international exam in English.
dp900.prep: Study with free Microsoft Learn materials. Free online training (Virtual Training Day) can give an exam discount. Students can also register through Certiport.

aws_aip.what: Basics of AI, machine learning and generative AI, and AWS AI services.
aws_aip.who: Anyone who wants to show AI knowledge with a certification known by Japanese IT companies.
aws_aip.prep: Use the free exam prep plan on AWS Skill Builder. Available in English, Japanese and more.

aws_mle.what: Building machine learning models and running them in production.
aws_mle.who: The next goal after AWS AI Practitioner — a goal after graduation.
aws_mle.prep: A new version (MLA-C02) is being introduced. Check the latest information on the official page.

gcp_mle.what: Designing, building and running AI systems on Google Cloud.
gcp_mle.who: People with work experience (3+ years recommended).
gcp_mle.prep: Use Google Cloud's official learning path and sample questions.

nac_net.what: Basics of how networks work (IP addresses, Wi-Fi, home networks). Score 70% or more on the final exam to earn a digital badge.
nac_net.who: Anyone new to networking. A first step before CCST or CCNA.
nac_net.prep: Sign up for free at Cisco Networking Academy and work through the course (about 22 hours), including Packet Tracer simulator activities.

nac_ai.what: An introduction to data science and AI. Many courses give a digital badge when you finish.
nac_ai.who: Anyone who wants to see the big picture of data science and AI in English.
nac_ai.prep: Sign up for free at Cisco Networking Academy and learn at your own pace.

ccst_net.what: Entry-level networking knowledge — the entrance to networking jobs.
ccst_net.who: Anyone aiming for a networking job. A first step toward CCNA.
ccst_net.prep: Prepare with free Cisco Networking Academy courses. The exam is 50 minutes, available in English, Japanese, Chinese and more.

lpic1.what: Basic Linux server operation and administration — the foundation for server, network and cloud work.
lpic1.who: Anyone who wants to work with servers or the cloud.
lpic1.prep: You must pass two exams, 101 and 102 (90 minutes, 60 questions each). Available in English, Japanese, Chinese and more.

ccna.what: A broad range: network fundamentals, configuration, IP connectivity, security and automation. One of the best-known networking certifications in the world.
ccna.who: Anyone aiming to be a network engineer. Highly valued by Japanese employers too.
ccna.prep: A 120-minute exam in English or Japanese. A new version (v2.0) is planned for February 2027, so check which version your study materials cover.

netplus.what: Vendor-neutral networking knowledge and troubleshooting skills.
netplus.who: Anyone who wants to prove networking basics that do not depend on one vendor.
netplus.prep: CompTIA recommends 9–12 months of hands-on experience. Up to 90 questions in 90 minutes, in English, Japanese and more.

ora_sql.what: Writing correct SQL on Oracle Database (queries, joins, adding and changing data, creating tables).
ora_sql.who: Anyone who wants to work with databases. A big next goal after our SQL practice site.
ora_sql.prep: 63 questions in 120 minutes; pass with 63%. In English or Japanese. The fee is high, so first check your skills with HackerRank SQL.

paiza_sql.what: A test on paiza, a Japanese service for IT engineers, that rates your SQL on 5 levels (beta since 2025). Level 2 covers conditions and basic aggregation — close to HackerRank SQL (Basic).
paiza_sql.who: Anyone who wants to work for a Japanese company. Japanese employers know paiza well, so the result is easy to explain in interviews.
paiza_sql.prep: Take it after signing up. The problems are in Japanese, so it is also Japanese reading practice. Build your basics with HackerRank first.

valH: Do free badges really help? What hiring people say
valLead: We collected opinions from recruiters and other learners around the world about free badges like HackerRank's. Know the good and the bad, and use them wisely.
good: They are free, and when you pass you get a certificate you can put on LinkedIn and your CV.
When a job ad asks for "SQL" or "Python", a badge is evidence checked by a third party. It is a plus, especially for new graduates and beginners.
Many companies use HackerRank for their own hiring tests. Practising here gets you used to the real test.
bad: Many data recruiters say they don't look at certificates much — they want to see real skills.
Some people say harshly that a badge is "just decoration on your profile".
A badge almost never lets you skip interviews or tests. Many people freeze when they have to write code in front of someone.
There are few questions, and some people pass by memorising answers. So a badge alone may not convince people of your real skill.
In Japan, many people still don't know this badge.
do: A badge is not the goal — it is your first step. After passing, move on to the next level or a full exam.
Don't memorise answers; learn to solve problems yourself. In interviews you will be asked how you thought when you wrote the SQL.
Show a project where you analysed data with SQL (a portfolio) together with the badge. "Badge + project + explaining" is a strong set.
When you apply to Japanese companies, explain in one sentence what the badge proves (e.g. "I passed a test solving 2 SQL problems in 30 minutes").
